forces.title: Increasing BTM BESS adoption for C&I and rooftop solar
forces.description: Distributed, customer-driven adoption of Behind-the-Meter (BTM) Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) is growing across Commercial & Industrial (C&I) users, data centers, telecom, and rooftop solar. This trend, supported by declining battery costs and evolving tariff structures, shifts beyond backup to include power quality, cost optimization, and resilience. This directly impacts Power Distribution & Retail Supply by changing consumption patterns, potentially reducing peak demand, and necessitating new grid management strategies for distributed energy resources.
forces.source_title: Why India's BESS growth story depends on delivering bankable projects

forces.title: Bharat Small Reactors for industrial and distributed power
forces.description: India is developing Bharat Small Reactors (BSRs) to provide captive, co-located, 24x7 firm power near industrial demand centers like ports, terminals, and data centers. These modular reactors, based on the 220 MW PHWR platform, are intended to extend nuclear power beyond traditional grid-scale generation into distributed and industrial applications. This represents a structural change for Power Distribution & Retail Supply, as it could reduce the reliance of large consumers on the distribution network and shift energy procurement dynamics.
forces.source_title: How India’s nuclear ambition can power the next global clean energy push

forces.title: RTC power supply eases DISCOM balancing act
forces.description: The mechanism for Round-The-Clock (RTC) power supply, which bundles electricity from conventional and non-conventional sources, is directly supplied to distribution companies (DISCOMs). This eliminates the need for DISCOMs to balance power fluctuations caused by intermittent renewable energy sources, thereby enhancing grid stability and operational efficiency for Power Distribution & Retail Supply. This development provides a significant tailwind by de-risking renewable integration at the distribution level.

forces.title: Decentralized solar improves DISCOM financial viability
forces.description: The implementation of decentralized solar plants, particularly under the government’s PM-KUSUM program, is proving beneficial for the Power Distribution & Retail Supply sector. By boosting farmer incomes and contributing to India's non-fossil power capacity targets, these initiatives also directly improve the financial viability of distribution companies (DISCOMs). This tailwind stems from better localized load management, reduced line losses, and potentially new revenue streams for DISCOMs through managing decentralized generation.

forces.title: Electricity rules empower consumers and modernize grid
forces.description: Amendments to the Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020, and the Draft National Electricity Policy (NEP) 2026 represent significant tailwinds for Power Distribution & Retail Supply. These rules facilitate faster rooftop solar installations and separate connections for electric vehicle charging, empowering consumers. Crucially, the policy also emphasizes grid modernization, deployment of energy storage systems, and improved financial viability of DISCOMs, directly aiming to ensure reliable and affordable power supply at the retail level.

forces.title: PM Surya Ghar Yojana boosts household rooftop solar
forces.description: The Government of India's PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana aims to install rooftop solar plants in one crore households by 2026-27, with over 40 lakh beneficiary households and 9.56 GW installed as of March 2026. This ambitious scheme is a major tailwind for Power Distribution & Retail Supply by promoting distributed renewable energy generation among retail consumers, reducing grid dependence, and fostering energy self-reliance. It requires DISCOMs to adapt to a more dynamic, bi-directional power flow and manage diverse consumer energy sources.

forces.title: Smart Meter National Programme drives demand for advanced metering
forces.description: India's Smart Meter National Programme, aiming to replace 250 million conventional electricity meters with smart meters, is a significant tailwind for the Power Distribution & Retail Supply sector. This large-scale deployment will modernize metering infrastructure, enhance billing accuracy, enable better load management for DISCOMs, and facilitate demand-side response. The program also has a mandated domestic value addition, encouraging local manufacturing and driving technological upgrades within the distribution segment.
forces.source_title: Wired for growth: India’s electrical-equipment opportunity

forces.title: High import dependence for smart meter subcomponents
forces.description: While India's Smart Meter National Programme aims for 60% domestic value addition, the sector faces a significant headwind from over 60% import dependence at the subcomponent level. Electronic components and communication chipsets, accounting for over 20% of the bill of materials for smart meters, are largely imported (over 80% from China, Japan, Taiwan). This reliance on foreign supply chains poses risks to cost competitiveness, supply security, and achieving full self-reliance for Power Distribution & Retail Supply infrastructure, potentially delaying deployment or increasing costs.
forces.source_title: Wired for growth: India’s electrical-equipment opportunity

viewpoints.title: India's BTM BESS adoption expanding beyond backup to energy management
viewpoints.description: EY-Parthenon observes a progressive shift in India's Behind-the-Meter (BTM) Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) adoption. Initially driven by reliability needs like backup for C&I, data centers, telecom, and rooftop solar, demand is now expanding towards power quality, cost optimization, and energy management applications. This trend is supported by falling battery costs and evolving tariff structures, leading to a resilient, adoption-driven growth in BTM BESS that impacts load management and consumer engagement for power distribution and retail supply.
viewpoints.source_title: Why India's BESS growth story depends on delivering bankable projects

viewpoints.title: Government policies strengthen DISCOM financial viability and consumer empowerment
viewpoints.description: IBEF highlights the positive impact of government initiatives, particularly the amendments to the Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020, and the Draft National Electricity Policy (NEP) 2026. These policies aim to empower consumers through faster rooftop solar installations and EV charging connections, while simultaneously focusing on large-scale renewable energy integration, energy storage deployment, grid modernization, and improved financial viability for DISCOMs. This concerted effort is expected to ensure reliable and affordable power supply, strengthening the Power Distribution & Retail Supply sector.

viewpoints.title: Electrical equipment industry poised for global leadership with coordinated effort
viewpoints.description: McKinsey views India's electrical equipment industry as having the potential to become a globally competitive manufacturing powerhouse, driven by domestic demand and structural advantages. With coordinated progress across competitiveness, technology, exports, and electronics/software, domestic production could scale to over $195 billion by 2035, shrinking import dependence by half. This positive outlook, particularly for segments like smart meters, suggests robust foundational support and technological advancements for the Power Distribution & Retail Supply sector, enabling better infrastructure and operational efficiency.
viewpoints.source_title: Wired for growth: India’s electrical-equipment opportunity

demand_drivers.description: Overall surge in electrification and scaling domestic demand in India drives the consumption of electrical equipment.
Specific demand for categories like cables and wires, transformers, and high- and low-voltage switchgear for modernizing and expanding T&D networks.

new_opportunities.description: The national program to replace 250 million conventional electricity meters with smart meters creates significant demand for advanced metering equipment and associated services.
